fields.description:
## CI failure

- Node: tests/test_plan_filter_query_canonical.py::test_canonical_query_round_trip_property

During pool-launch-reservation verification on 2026-08-24, the full just test-scoped lane failed this node with Hypothesis FailedHealthCheck: Input generation is slow. Reproduction: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_plan_filter_query_canonical.py::test_canonical_query_round_trip_property --hypothesis-seed=102085564666404071502811727305596672010 -q. The isolated rerun on the same tree also failed with the same too_slow health check after only two valid inputs, so this is a deterministic test failure rather than a full-lane-only flake. The local diff touches LLM model-alias reservation/redemption and validator syntax, not plan filter query canonicalization or its Hypothesis strategies.

evidence.note: During conflict-repair verification at HEAD c09fe5170, just check escalated to the full suite and failed tests/test_vcs_log_filter_query.py::test_canonical_query_round_trip_property with Hypothesis FailedHealthCheck too_slow. The exact node reproduced in a serial failed-subset rerun on the same tree with .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q; unlike the two plan-approval failures from the full run, this one did not pass on rerun. The memory-priority conflict repair does not touch VCS log filter query generation.

payload.entry: NEGATIVE REPRODUCTION from the sase-sq land agent (master 39bc4bc70 plus this turn's landing diff). Phase bead sase-sq.3 left a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP for tests/test_vcs_log_filter_query.py::test_canonical_query_round_trip_property failing Hypothesis FailedHealthCheck (input generation too slow), confirmed pre-existing via git stash at the time. Routing it here rather than filing a duplicate: this bead already owns the too_slow health check for test_canonical_query_round_trip_property, and 0cx's +1 names the exact tests/test_vcs_log_filter_query.py node. I did not reproduce it and am therefore recording a note rather than a +1: '.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_vcs_log_filter_query.py::test_canonical_query_round_trip_property -p no:randomly -q' passes in 0.47s (1 passed in 3.49s), the node has no entry in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt, and the test carries a bare @given with no suppress_health_check. That is consistent with a load-dependent health check rather than a deterministic failure, so the isolated-rerun-also-fails evidence in this bead's description is the stronger signal and this note only adds that the node is green on an unloaded host at this HEAD.
